C-SESSION-DURABILITY.Name: Session durability: proven close-after-write commit, tri-state recently-closed checks, one-request one-stat-pass restore reads, a write-path position cap, and a regression net aimed at the shipped cold-start contract
C-SESSION-DURABILITY.Summary: The session profile survives writes, closes and restarts on faith in four places plus one stale net. (1) The close-time session commit is bounded but unproven: no test at any layer demonstrates that the window closes after the session write settles, that the per-tab reading-position flushes riding the same commit are inside the confirmation window, or what an injected slow write does to the close — e2e has zero close/session-write coverage. (2) The recently-closed history treats ANY stat failure as a confirmed deletion: a transient IPC or permission error silently erases a recoverable entry, and the vitest suite actively pins that behavior. (3) The restore path reads the four-key profile with four sequential preference round-trips, stats every saved path one-by-one interleaved with opens, and finds each tab's format record by a linear scan inside the open loop. (4) The position-store size cap (200) is enforced only on the read path, so the on-disk store can silently outgrow its bound between reads. (5) The e2e net still remembers the pre-C-FIX-009 cold-start defect as a test.fixme asserting behavior that is no longer reachable, and a manual regression entry sits stale at "pending — FIX-009 open". This change proves the close-after-write contract at unit and e2e level (shim-injected slow, never-settling and rejected mt_prefs_set_many; per-tab position flushes explicitly inside the confirmation scope) without touching the predecessor's owner-confirmed two-second bound; ports the filePositionStore tri-state stat verdict into recentlyClosed so an entry is dropped only when its file is confirmed gone (MT_FS_NOT_FOUND / isFile:false), transient failures keeping the entry behind their own localized notice; adds the read-batch mirror of the write batch (mt_prefs_get_many / ipcPrefs.getMany) so the live restore reads the profile in ONE request and checks all saved paths in ONE concurrent stat pass before the first open; indexes the per-tab format lookup into a Map; applies MAX_POSITION_FILES on the save path; and re-aims the stale nets (affordance-audit fixme, regression-tests wel-002) at the shipped C-FIX-009 cold-start contract. The write-frequency residue of the session profile (one pref set = one full store-file save) stays a recorded residue of C-SESSION-WRITE-ATOMICITY, not relitigated here.

Problem.Description: (1) Close-after-write is unproven (high). The predecessor C-SESSION-WRITE-ATOMICITY (applied 2026-11-21) already bound the quit/window-close session write: prepareCommit routes quit/window-close to _boundedSessionCommit (src/renderer/src/store/editor.js:504-505), which races _saveSessionState against a fixed SESSION_COMMIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 2000 timer (editor.js:76, :628-649) and logs honest markers (BLOCK_SESSION_COMMIT_TIMEOUT, BLOCK_SESSION_WRITE_FAILED). But the ordering contract — close happens after the write settles, or the bound fires and the close proceeds honestly while the single-transaction backend keeps a torn-free generation — is demonstrated nowhere: documentOperations.test.js holds three renderer stubs (close_waits_for_session_write_confirmation_before_destroy :261, bounded_timeout_still_closes_honestly :282, rejected_session_write_still_closes :300) driven by a mocked ipcPrefs, and tests/e2e contains no close/session-write coverage at all (the only close-adjacent spec, tests/e2e/perf/characterization-save-close.spec.ts, is renderer-only characterization that explicitly does not cover real IPC or disk bytes). The per-tab reading-position flushes that ride _saveSessionState (editor.js:725-728, the C-FILE-POSITION-MEMORY corner C-7 contract) have no pin proving they complete inside the awaited confirmation window, so a reorder that orphans them after the destroy would pass every suite. (2) recentlyClosed deletes on any stat failure. REOPEN_ONE stats the entry's path and maps any rejection to exists=false → CONSUME (src/renderer/src/store/recentlyClosed.js:114-120, the consume at :122); REOPEN_ALL stats every entry with .catch(() => false) and drops the false ones up front (recentlyClosed.js:168-176). A transient failure (EACCES, an evicted volume, an IPC hiccup) therefore permanently deletes a recoverable entry — the exact defect class already fixed in the sibling module: filePositionStore's tri-state verdict (true / false=confirmed-not-a-file including the MT_FS_NOT_FOUND code / undefined=cannot-tell, filePositionStore.js:209-237) prunes only on a confirmed false, pinned by tests/renderer/util/file-position-store.test.js:206, :229, :255. The vitest net pins the wrong behavior: tests/renderer/store/recently-closed.test.js:135-142 and :173-191 assert the drop on generic Error('not found') rejections that carry no NOT_FOUND code. (3) Restore reads are unbatched and unindexed. The live restore path reads the profile with four sequential awaits — readList('lastSessionFolders'), readList('lastSessionTabs'), ipcPrefs.get('lastSessionActive'), ipcPrefs.get('lastSessionFormats') (editor.js:828-831); the cold-start capture reads the same four keys in parallel Promise.all (editor.js:779-784); there is no read-batch command — the backend exposes mt_prefs_get, mt_prefs_set, mt_prefs_set_many and mt_prefs_get_all (src-tauri/src/m005_prefs.rs:399, :412, :442-461, :464; facade src/renderer/src/ipc/runtime/prefs.ts:21-47 has get/set/setMany/getAll, no getMany), so the write batch got its mirror and the read did not. Existence checks fire one-by-one interleaved with opens: exists() stats each folder (editor.js:842-851) and each file (:852-853 via the helper :820-827) sequentially inside the open loops. The per-tab format record is found by formats.find inside the same loop (editor.js:855) — O(N²) on restore. (4) The size cap is read-only. MAX_POSITION_FILES = 200 (filePositionStore.js:55) is applied by capStoreFiles only in loadFilePosition's read path (filePositionStore.js:271-283); saveFilePosition (:289-306) writes without counting, so the on-disk store can silently exceed the bound until the next read repairs it. (5) The cold-start net is stale. C-FIX-009-SESSION-COLD-START (applied, shipped v2.7.0) rebound the welcome "Last session" row to the boot-time frozen offer: the row renders only when this launch skipped auto-restore (restoreSessionOnLaunch off — default is on, store/preferences.js:382) and the frozen boot snapshot is non-empty, the click restores the frozen payload via RESTORE_SESSION({ from }) without rereading live preferences (editor.js:805-831), and a restore that opens nothing raises a visible notice (src/renderer/src/components/recent/index.vue:555-571). The net never caught up: tests/e2e/affordance-audit.spec.ts:407-416 still carries test.fixme «Last session row restores the closed session (FIX-009)» with an "open"-era comment and a body asserting the pre-fix reachability (row from the live preference), and its welcome beforeEach (:340-361) still stubs mt_prefs_get to serve lastSessionTabs from the live preference; tests/regression-tests.json:29 (wel-002) sits at status "pending" with the note «FIX-009 open (2026-10-20) — reported broken; verify after its repair».

Goals.R-1: CLOSE-AFTER-WRITE (scout key 18, high): the close-after-write ordering becomes proven coverage, not untested code, with the predecessor's binding shape unchanged. The confirmation scope is made explicit and pinned: the commit awaited by the window-close barrier (prepareCommit → _boundedSessionCommit, editor.js:504-505, :628-649) covers the batched profile write AND the per-tab position flushes that _saveSessionState runs after the batch (editor.js:725-728) — a named unit pin proves the flushes complete before the close command is invoked, so a reorder that orphans them behind the destroy can no longer pass. The e2e layer gains its first close/session-write evidence through the existing tauri-shim seams (window.__mockInvoke override + window.__invokeLog, tests/e2e/fixtures/tauri-shim.ts:209-222, the update-notice.spec.ts injection pattern): a NEW spec injects a slow mt_prefs_set_many handler and proves with a controlled settling sentinel that mt_close_window is invoked only after the write settled (under the bound); a never-settling handler proves the two-second bound fires, the BLOCK_SESSION_COMMIT_TIMEOUT marker is logged, and the close still completes; a rejecting handler proves the close completes with BLOCK_SESSION_WRITE_FAILED surfaced. The bound's value and the timeout-still-closes trade — «wait at most two seconds, then honest markers and a torn-free on-disk generation either way» — are the predecessor's owner-confirmed decisions and stand unchanged; this goal adds the proof, the flush-inclusive scope, and nothing else.
Goals.R-2: STAT-TRI-STATE (scout key 17): recentlyClosed drops an entry only when its file is CONFIRMED gone. The tri-state verdict discipline of filePositionStore (filePositionStore.js:209-237) is ported: a stat answers true (isFile), false (confirmed not-a-file — isFile:false, or a rejection carrying the MT_FS_NOT_FOUND code), or undefined (cannot tell — any other rejection such as EACCES/evicted volume, no stat capability, or a flagless answer). REOPEN_ONE (recentlyClosed.js:112-146) consumes the entry only on a false verdict; a cannot-tell verdict keeps the entry, opens nothing, resolves false, and surfaces its own localized notice (new recent.recentlyClosed.* keys, all ten locales — the transient state must not borrow the confirmed-missing copy «{name} is no longer available»); a confirmed-missing verdict keeps today's exact behavior (drop + the existing missingNotice + basename-only marker). REOPEN_ALL (recentlyClosed.js:163-216) keeps its single concurrent stat pass but classifies with the same verdict: confirmed-missing entries are dropped up front and counted in missing (existing notice unchanged); cannot-tell entries are neither opened nor consumed, stay in the list for the next attempt, and are reported by their own localized notice — the return shape keys stay exactly { reopened, missing, active } with missing counting confirmed-missing only. The stale pins are unfolded in the same suites: recently-closed.test.js:135-142 and :173-191 drop-path coverage is re-pinned on NOT_FOUND-coded rejections, and new pins hold the transient-keeps-entry contract.
Goals.R-3: ONE-REQUEST RESTORE READS AND ONE STAT PASS (scout keys 15 + 13): the live session restore reads the profile as ONE request and checks existence in ONE pass. Backend: a new read-batch command mt_prefs_get_many(keys) in m005_prefs.rs — one mutex acquisition, read-only (no save, no generation change, no broadcast), returning a map of exactly the requested keys with absent keys as null (preserving the facade's null-for-absent semantics), registered in main.rs alongside mt_prefs_set_many — the deliberate mirror of the write batch, so the restore payload travels in one round-trip without hauling the whole store the way mt_prefs_get_all would. Facade: ipcPrefs.getMany (raw invoke per the setMany precedent, outside the typed M-013-A contract). Renderer: RESTORE_SESSION's live path (editor.js:828-831 — four sequential gets) becomes one getMany for the four lastSession* keys; the BOOT_SESSION cold-start capture (editor.js:779-784) shares the same one-request read if the plan finds it organic; the frozen-payload path (RESTORE_SESSION({ from }), the C-FIX-009 contract) keeps reading no preferences at all. Existence: all folder and file stats are hoisted into ONE concurrent pass before the first open (today's exists() fires sequentially per folder editor.js:842-851 and per file :852-853 interleaved with opens) — the scout's «one stat pass at open», folded into this read-batch goal renderer-side; the skip/notice semantics of C-MULTI-SOURCE-WORKSPACE are unchanged. No backend stat-batch command is built for this.
Goals.R-4: FORMAT MAP INDEX (scout key 16): the per-tab format lookup on restore stops being O(N²): the formats list is indexed into a Map by pathname once and the open loop's formats.find (editor.js:855) becomes an O(1) lookup. Pure renderer refactor, behavior-preserving: every existing format-restore pin (named pending formats, invalid-record rejection, frozen-offer formats) keeps passing byte-identically.
Goals.R-5: SIZE-CAP-ON-WRITE (scout key 14): the MAX_POSITION_FILES cap (200) is enforced on the write path too: saveFilePosition (filePositionStore.js:289-306) caps the store with the existing capStoreFiles (:107, newest-by-savedAt kept) before writing, the same discipline the read path already applies (:271-283), so the on-disk store can never silently exceed the bound between reads. The serialized mutation queue, the failed-read abort (no write derived from a failed read) and the return contracts are unchanged. The lastSession* profile keys stay uncapped by design — they are bounded by the user's real open tabs, and profile-content redesign is out of scope (NonGoals).
Goals.R-6: LAST-SESSION-TRUTH (scout key 19): the cold-start net is re-aimed at the shipped C-FIX-009 contract. The affordance-audit fixme (tests/e2e/affordance-audit.spec.ts:407-416) is rewritten as a real, passing test with the harness moved to the contract shape (restoreSessionOnLaunch=false at boot, the welcome.spec.ts:77/:103 stub pattern, replacing the live-preference stub at :340-361): the row renders only when auto-restore was skipped AND the frozen boot offer is non-empty (selectors unchanged: .welcome-screen .row-session, .row-name); the click restores the frozen offer and the editor becomes visible (.editor-with-tabs); a boot with an empty snapshot renders no row. The nothing-restored click notice (recent/index.vue:555-571) stays covered by the existing unit net (editor-session-coldstart.test.js), which keeps passing. tests/regression-tests.json wel-002 (:29) stops being a stale orphan: the «FIX-009 open (2026-10-20)» note is removed, the entry points at the rewritten e2e test as its automating cover, and its status fields are stamped from the implementation bundle's verification evidence instead of the permanent-pending state.
Goals.R-7: Governance: the touched governed files get VERSION bumps and CHANGE_SUMMARY entries per the modification checklist; the graph and verification deltas (.grace/graph/runtime.xml, .grace/verification/runtime.xml) land in the same bundle as the code, strictly on the M-005/M-011 and V-M-005/V-M-011 entries, with scenarios naming the new tests; no version change, release, tag or publication is authorized by this specification.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Tri-state recently-closed (failing-first): before the fix, a generic stat rejection drops the entry; after, tests/renderer/store/recently-closed.test.js pins reopen_one_keeps_the_entry_when_the_stat_verdict_is_cannot_tell (an EACCES-class rejection keeps the entry, invokes no mt::open-file, resolves false, and shows the new transient notice — not the confirmed-missing copy), reopen_all_keeps_transient_entries_and_counts_only_confirmed_missing (transient entries retained, excluded from missing, reported by the new notice; confirmed-missing still dropped and counted), reopen_one_still_drops_on_confirmed_not_found and the REOPEN_ALL twin (NOT_FOUND-coded rejections keep the exact today behavior), and the default checker's code-mapping pin mirrors file-position-store.test.js:229/:255; the stale pins at :135-142 and :173-191 are unfolded to the coded-rejection drop path without losing their drop coverage.

Write-path cap (failing-first): before the fix, saveFilePosition persists an over-cap store; after, tests/renderer/util/file-position-store.test.js pins saveFilePosition_caps_the_store_to_MAX_POSITION_FILES (a save into a store beyond 200 entries persists at most MAX_POSITION_FILES, newest-by-savedAt kept, ties deterministic) while the existing read-path cap/prune/queue pins (:119, :144, :178) stay green unchanged.

Read batch (failing-first): before the fix, no read-batch command exists; after, m005_prefs.rs pins get_many_returns_requested_keys_without_persisting (the map carries exactly the requested keys, absent keys as null, no store-file write and no generation change — asserted through the injected-rename seam discipline that the set_many pins :632/:717 established), main.rs registers it, and tests/renderer/store/session-restore.test.js pins restore_reads_the_session_profile_in_one_batched_get_many (the live RESTORE_SESSION issues exactly ONE ipcPrefs.getMany carrying the four lastSession* keys and NO per-key ipcPrefs.get for any of them — the mirror of the batched-write pin at :142-166) plus a_frozen_payload_restore_reads_no_preferences (the C-FIX-009 frozen path stays preference-free); the boot-gate and degradation pins keep passing.
